topStories.headline: Clement Street's Quieter End Is Filling Up Fast — but an Appeal Looms Over the Corridor
topStories.dek: A wave of new businesses is transforming the lower stretch of Clement Street near Arguello, even as the Therapy Stores planning fight may not be finished.
topStories.body:
The block of Clement Street running from Arguello Boulevard to Sixth Avenue is in the middle of a striking commercial makeover, with five new businesses either open or announced for addresses that were recently empty. A pilates and wellness studio called MNT Studio held a preview week at 35 Clement beginning October 19 and moved to its regular schedule on October 26. Kitchen Commons — a cookware shop and cafe backed by Liholiho Yacht Club co-owner Jeff Hanak and former Nopalito chef Connor Bruce — has been announced for 130 Clement this fall. Two cafe concepts, Evermore at 200 Clement and a fifth Cafe Réveille location at 324 Clement, are also in the pipeline for later this year.

The burst of activity comes in the wake of San Francisco's Planning Commission voting unanimously on September 24 to grant Therapy Stores a conditional use permit to open at 32 Clement, near Second Avenue. Therapy, a Bay Area gift-shop chain owned by Jing Chen, triggered the city's formula retail rules because planning code counted it as having 11 locations when it applied. The Clement Street Merchants Association, which posted 'No formula retail on Clement Street' fliers up and down the corridor and gathered roughly 400 signatures against the application, indicated it was actively considering an appeal to the Board of Supervisors within the 30-day window following the ruling.

With Clement Street's vacancy rate sitting below five percent — low even by citywide standards — the corridor is one of the healthiest retail strips on San Francisco's west side. Whether the Therapy Stores permit survives a potential supervisorial appeal, and how the new daytime-focused businesses reshape foot traffic on the block, will be the story to watch through the end of the year.

topStories.headline: Two Months After a Devastating Break-In, Modern Relics Won't Reopen as a Jewelry Store
topStories.dek: Inner Richmond jeweler Alix Blüh, whose Cabrillo Street shop was ransacked in August, is now considering turning the space into a community gallery — and no arrests have been made.
topStories.body:
For two decades, Modern Relics occupied a quiet residential stretch of Cabrillo Street near Ninth Avenue, where owner and jewelry designer Alix Blüh made and sold bespoke pieces from a loft studio above an antique-filled ground-floor gallery. On the morning of August 13, Blüh walked from her nearby home to find the front door pried open, display cases smashed, and the metal locker holding her most valuable work emptied. She estimates total losses — including finished jewelry, gold and gemstone raw materials, antique display cases, and property damage — at between $200,000 and $300,000.

The Richmond Review reported on October 26 that no arrests have been made. The San Francisco Police Department's Richmond Station responded to the shop that morning, and the investigation remains open. Blüh has said the business she built over 20 years will not return in its current form as a high-end jewelry store. She has indicated publicly that she hopes to reopen the Cabrillo Street space as early as 2027 as a gallery for other artists, potentially centered on a clay studio. 'What I'm really excited to do is turn this space and repurpose it for the community,' she told Mission Local in September.

topStories.headline: Clement Street Trick-or-Treats Saturday; Outer Balboa Celebrates Día de Muertos on Sunday
topStories.dek: Merchants on two Richmond corridors are anchoring a neighborhood-wide Halloween and Día de Muertos weekend, with the Balboa Theater adding a mystery movie marathon for good measure.
topStories.body:
The Richmond is packing its Halloween and Día de Muertos observances into back-to-back days this weekend. On Saturday, October 31, the Clement Street Merchants Association is organizing a daytime trick-or-treating crawl along the Inner Richmond corridor, with participating businesses stocked with candy for families and children. At Fifth Avenue off Clement, neighbors have constructed a pop-up fan shrine to the Golden State Warriors, cheekily christened 'Boohalla,' adding a local flourish to the route.

On Sunday, November 1, Outer Balboa Street between 35th and 36th Avenues hosts a Día de Muertos celebration from noon to 4 p.m. The event is a joint production of Outer Richmond merchants — including Chino's, Simple Pleasures cafe, Noise Records, and the Eye & Hand Society — alongside the Richmond Neighborhood Center and Supervisor Connie Chan's office. Organizers plan community altars for the dead, cultural performances, and family-friendly activities throughout the afternoon.

For those who prefer their scares on screen, the Balboa Theater is running a Halloween-day mystery movie marathon quadruple feature on October 31, with tickets priced at $13.

moreNews.headline: Governor's El Niño Emergency Declaration Puts Richmond and Presidio Residents on Notice
moreNews.body: District 1 Supervisor Connie Chan's October 26 column in the Richmond Review flagged Governor Gavin Newsom's September 21 state of emergency declaration aimed at boosting preparedness for a forecast strong El Niño winter storm season. For residents of the Richmond and Presidio neighborhoods — where low-lying avenues can be vulnerable to runoff — the declaration is a timely prompt to review home drainage and check city flood-preparedness resources before the rains arrive.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club
